text:
Asha Patel: Quick tax/ops q — Im 51 and expecting a large year-end bonus paid as a supplemental check. I want to max out 50+ catch-up deferrals and also increase pre-tax deferrals on the bonus. Does payroll apply my regular % to supplemental checks or do I need to set a special election? Also Im switching from individual -> family HDHP on Sep 1  does HSA catch-up for 55+ change if I change coverage?

Jordan Li (Payroll): Congrats on the bonus! Two parts: supplemental pay often uses a separate payroll code. We default supplemental deferral to your current elective deferral %, but some payroll systems require a separate election for supplemental/bonus. If you want a different %, submit a one-off deferral change now and indicate "apply to supplemental" in the note.

Maya Gomez (Benefits): On catch-up: employees 50+ can contribute the additional catch-up amount to the 401(k) above the standard deferral limit. That catch-up is still payroll-withheld; you must ensure year-to-date withholding + planned bonus withholdings dont exceed the calendar-year IRS limits. If you want to front-load catch-up on the bonus, set the catch-up amount as a fixed-dollar per-pay election or increase % for the pay that includes the bonus.

Asha Patel: How does employer match treat bonuses? Is match calculated on supplemental pay?

Jordan Li (Payroll): Match applies to eligible compensation as defined in the plan. Bonus/supplemental pay is typically eligible unless the plan excludes it. Match is calculated on the actual deferral taken on that pay. So if you defer on the bonus, match will be applied for that pay period per the plan formula.

Fidelity Support: Recordkeeper note: "To maximize catch-up on a single supplemental check, use a fixed-dollar deferral that does not exceed the elective deferral limit when combined with prior deferrals. All employee pre-tax and catch-up deferrals must originate from payroll withholding. We cannot accept after-the-fact pre-tax deposits for missed payroll withholding."

Maya Gomez (Benefits): Practical steps: 1) Tell payroll the bonus pay date so they can prepare the payroll override. 2) Submit a Benefits Portal election indicating the exact % or $ amount for the bonus pay (label as "supplemental pay election"). 3) Monitor YTD deferrals in the portal so we dont exceed limits.

Asha Patel: About HSA: Im 55 and will switch to family HDHP Sep 1. Catch-up contribution for HSA (55+) is allowed?

Maya Gomez (Benefits): HSAs have a separate 55+ catch-up amount ($1,000 standard in recent years) and that remains available regardless of switching coverage midyear as long as you are HSA-eligible at the time of contribution. Coverage tier affects the HSA contribution limit (individual vs family) prorated by months of coverage. Example: if you're on individual Jan-Aug and family Sep-Dec, you get 8 months of individual + 4 months of family proration for the calendar year. The 55+ catch-up is not prorated; you can contribute the full catch-up amount if eligible.

Asha Patel: So I could hit the full HSA family limit + the 55+ catch-up even though family coverage starts in Sep?

Fidelity Support: Clarification: HSA annual family limit is prorated by months of family coverage. The 55+ catch-up is separate and not prorated. If you want to attempt the family full limit for months you werent on family coverage, that would exceed IRS rules. Use benefits@redwood.com and provide coverage dates and we will calculate exact max allowable contribution.

Jordan Li (Payroll): Also note payroll can only withhold HSA per-pay period when you are enrolled and active on payroll. If you want to accelerate contributions after Sep 1 to reach prorated family limit, set a higher per-pay-dollar HSA election once family coverage is active.

Asha Patel: Any impact on FSA if Im switching? I have a limited-purpose FSA now.

Maya Gomez (Benefits): If you keep limited-purpose FSA (LPFSA) you can still contribute to an HSA. If you switch to a general-purpose FSA, that would make you ineligible to contribute to HSA for overlapping months. Make sure to elect LPFSA if you want concurrent HSA. We can change FSA type at open enrollment or qualifying life event if allowed.

hr-bot: Policy note (automated): "401(k) catch-up contributions (age 50+) and HSA catch-ups follow IRS rules and must be done via payroll withholding. Supplemental/bonus elections may use a separate payroll code and require explicit election. Contact benefits@redwood.com to verify prorated HSA limits and payroll@redwood.com to set supplemental withholding."

Asha Patel: Thanks all  Ill email payroll the bonus date and cc benefits for HSA proration calc. Appreciate the quick help :+1:
